---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send, update, and delete messages, list channels and users, read conversation history and threads, and manage reactions. Use when Gemini CLI needs to post to or read from a Slack workspace using a bot (xoxb-) or user (xoxp-) token.
---

# Slack API

Work with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API. Every operation needs a bot or user token and returns JSON with an `ok` flag.

## Authentication

- Read the token from the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable, or pass `--token` explicitly. Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`.
- Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- If no token is available or requests return `invalid_auth`, stop and tell the user to set `SLACK_TOKEN`.

## Preferred method: use the wrapper script

Use `scripts/slack_api.cjs` instead of writing fetch/curl code from scratch:

```bash
# Send a message
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --data '{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Deploy finished"}'

# List channels
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list --method GET --data '{"types": "public_channel,private_channel", "limit": 200}'

# Read message history, following pagination, capped at 100 items
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history --method GET --data '{"channel": "C1234567890", "limit": 200}' --paginate --max-items 100
```

Options: `--method GET|POST` (default POST), `--data '{"json": ...}'`, `--paginate` (follow `next_cursor`), `--max-items N` (truncate long arrays), `--token TOKEN`, `--dry-run` (print the request without sending).

The script prints the response as compact JSON on success and `ERROR <code>` on failure (exit 1). Always verify the `ok` field.

## Workflow

1. **Resolve names to IDs.** List channels with `conversations.list` (or use `conversations.info` with an ID) and users with `users.list`; match by `name`/`real_name`. Prefer IDs over names in later calls.
2. **Post.** Use `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (ID preferred), `text`, optional `blocks`, and `thread_ts` to reply in a thread.
3. **Read.** Use `conversations.history` for channel messages and `conversations.replies` for threads. Remember `ts` values are strings like `1700000000.123456`.
4. **Act on results.** Update (`chat.update`), delete (`chat.delete`), or react (`reactions.add`) using the message `ts`.

## Error handling

- Every response has `ok`; when `false`, the `error` field holds a code such as `invalid_auth`, `channel_not_found`, `not_in_channel`, or `missing_scope`.
- On HTTP 429 (`rate_limited`), respect the `Retry-After` header and back off.
- `not_in_channel` means the bot must join first: `conversations.join` (public channels only).
- `missing_scope` means the token lacks a required scope; tell the user which scope is needed.

## Reference

For exact parameters, payload examples, and scope requirements, read [references/api.md](references/api.md).

# Slack API Reference

## Table of contents

- [Conventions](#conventions)
- [Messaging (chat.*)](#messaging-chat)
- [Channels and conversations (conversations.*)](#channels-and-conversations-conversations)
- [Users (users.*)](#users-users)
- [Reactions (reactions.*)](#reactions-reactions)
- [Common error codes](#common-error-codes)
- [Scopes](#scopes)
- [Notes](#notes)

## Conventions

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`; all calls return JSON.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`.
- Every response has an `ok` boolean. When `false`, the `error` field contains a code.
- Request bodies are `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; nested objects/arrays are JSON-encoded as string values.
- Pagination: pass `cursor` from `response_metadata.next_cursor`; an empty string means no more pages. `limit` is capped at 200.

## Messaging (chat.*)

### chat.postMessage
Send a message to a channel or thread.

| Param | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `channel` | Channel/user ID, or name |
| `text` | Message text (mrkdwn supported) |
| `blocks` | JSON array of Block Kit blocks |
| `thread_ts` | Parent message ts to reply in a thread |
| `as_user` | `true` to post as the user (user tokens) |
| `link_names` | `true` to linkify channel/user names |
| `username`, `icon_emoji`, `icon_url` | Override bot identity (needs `chat:write.customize`) |

Response includes `ts` (message timestamp) and `channel`.

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Deploy finished",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Deploy finished* :white_check_mark:" }
    }
  ]
}
```

### chat.update / chat.delete
Params: `channel` and `ts` (required for both); `text`/`blocks` for updates. Returns the new `ts`.

### chat.postEphemeral
Params: `channel`, `user`, `text` (optional `blocks`). Message visible only to the specified user.

## Channels and conversations (conversations.*)

### conversations.list
List channels the token can see.

| Param | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `types` | Comma-separated: `public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` |
| `exclude_archived` | `true` to hide archived channels |
| `limit` | 1-200 (default 100) |
| `cursor` | Pagination cursor |

Response: `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_archived`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `num_members`, `topic`, `purpose`.

### conversations.info
Params: `channel`. Response: `channel`.

### conversations.history
Fetch message history of a channel or DM.

| Param | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `channel` | Required |
| `limit` | 1-200 (default 100) |
| `cursor` | Pagination cursor |
| `oldest` / `latest` | Unix timestamps; `inclusive` controls boundary inclusion |

Response: `messages[]` with `type`, `user`, `text`, `ts`, `thread_ts`, `reply_count`, `blocks`, `subtype` (e.g. `channel_join`, `bot_message`, `channel_archive`).

### conversations.replies
Params: `channel`, `ts` (parent message). Returns the parent message plus all replies.

### conversations.create / conversations.rename / conversations.archive
`conversations.create` takes `name` (no leading `#`) and optional `is_private`. Rename/archive take `channel`.

### conversations.join / conversations.leave
Params: `channel`. Joining works for public channels; private channels require an invite.

## Users (users.*)

### users.list
Params: `limit`, `cursor`. Response: `members[]` with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `deleted`, `is_bot`.

### users.info
Params: `user`. Response: `user`.

### users.lookupByEmail
Params: `email`. Response: `user`.

## Reactions (reactions.*)

### reactions.add / reactions.remove
Params: `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp`.

### reactions.get
Params: `channel`, `timestamp`. Response: `message.reactions[]` with `name`, `count`, `users`.

## Common error codes

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Bad or missing token | Check SLACK_TOKEN |
| `channel_not_found` | Bad channel ID/name | Resolve with `conversations.list` |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not in the channel | `conversations.join` (public) or ask for an invite |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a required scope | Add the scope listed in the error |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429, too many requests | Wait for the `Retry-After` header |
| `name_taken` / `invalid_name` | Channel naming problem | Use a unique, valid name |
| `already_reacted` | Reaction already present | No-op; treat as success |
| `message_not_found` | Bad `ts` | Verify the message timestamp |

## Scopes

Bot tokens need scopes granted when installing the app:

- `chat:write` — send/update/delete messages
- `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` — read channels/DMs
- `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` — read history
- `channels:manage` — create/rename/archive public channels
- `channels:join` — join public channels
- `users:read` — list and look up users
- `reactions:write`, `reactions:read` — manage reactions

## Notes

- `ts` values are float strings like `1700000000.123456`. Always pass them as strings, never as numbers (precision loss).
- Channel names are unique per workspace and must not contain a leading `#`.
- `text` supports mrkdwn: bold `*text*`, italic `_text_`, code `` `code` ``, emoji `:emoji:`.
- For file uploads, use the `files.upload` endpoint with multipart/form-data (not supported by the wrapper script's form encoding).
